title: The Sixteenth Yearbook
premise: Xanthe Crane, a scholarship student counting down to graduation at Ashgrove Academy, discovers his late grandmother's recipe box contains ritual instructions instead of recipes — directions for the Founders' Audition, a secret tradition that has quietly chosen the town's leaders for a century. Pulled into the audition by the very people who engineered his scholarship, Xanthe learns his grandmother was its last honest judge, and that the current stewards have corrupted the rite to hoard power and erase inconvenient memories. To survive the final audition, he must restore the tradition's original purpose — choosing servants of the town rather than masters of it — even if it means sacrificing the inheritance that could have made him untouchable.
about_author: S. M. Okafor is a former boarding school archivist who grew up in a small town where everyone knew which families 'mattered' and no one said why. They write young adult fiction about inheritance — the kind written in wills, and the kind written in silence.

chapters.title: Counting Days
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Establishes Ashgrove Academy's rigid hierarchy: legacy students glide, scholarship students serve. Xanthe endures a humiliating work-study shift while memorizing the days left until graduation. Emotional beat: weary resignation sharpened by quiet defiance.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Sorting his late grandmother's belongings, he finds her recipe box — but cards labeled 'First Course,' 'Second Course' contain instructions for gathering names, dates, and objects, not ingredients. The last card reads: 'Finish it, or they finish the town.' Emotional beat: grief curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Ashgrove Remembers Wrong
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. He tests one card's instructions at the town archive and finds records altered — founding dates shifted, a fire that never happened. Legacy classmate Odile Voss catches him and, instead of reporting him, warns him to stop looking. Emotional beat: first vertigo of unreality.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Headmaster Lark's POV. Lark reveals the Academy has watched Xanthe since enrollment; his scholarship was payment for his grandmother's service as an Audition judge. He formally invites Xanthe into this year's Founders' Audition. Emotional beat: gilded menace — flattery as a leash.

chapters.title: Sixteen Names
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Sixteen seniors are summoned; each receives a sealed course card. Xanthe recognizes his grandmother's handwriting on all of them — decades old, distributed like scripture. He allies reluctantly with Odile, who admits she's competed before, under different rules. Emotional beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: First Course: Salt
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The first trial asks contestants to give up something seasoned with memory — Xanthe surrenders a recording of his grandmother's voice. Afterward he can't recall her laugh. Emotional beat: horror at what the tradition actually consumes.

chapters.title: What the Town Forgot
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Researching the altered archives, he finds a photograph of his grandmother with six other judges, four faces scratched out. A retired groundskeeper tells him the Audition once chose stewards who served; now it chooses owners. Emotional beat: righteous anger taking root.

chapters.title: Second Course: Bread
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Contestants must break bread with someone they intend to surpass — a loyalty test disguised as ambition. Xanthe refuses to betray his friend Milo and passes only because Odile covers for him. Emotional beat: the cost of integrity inside a corrupt game.

chapters.title: Lark's Ledger
chapters.summary: Headmaster Lark's POV. Lark reviews the ledger of past Auditions, noting how winners' families consolidated land, water rights, and the school board itself. He justifies it as stability — towns need shepherds. Emotional beat: chilling self-persuasion; corruption as caretaking.

chapters.title: Third Course: Bitter Herbs
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The trial forces contestants to name a grievance against another contestant publicly. Odile is ordered to denounce Xanthe; she does, half-heartedly, and hates herself for it. Their alliance fractures. Emotional beat: shame and the machinery of division exposed.

chapters.title: The Scratched-Out Faces
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. He identifies three erased judges — all dead within a year of trying to reform the Audition. His grandmother survived by hiding the true final course inside the recipe box. Emotional beat: understanding his inheritance is a mission, not a gift.

chapters.title: Milo's Price
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Milo, desperate for a scholarship of his own, informs on Xanthe's archive visits to Lark. Confronted, Milo breaks down: the system makes informants of everyone. Emotional beat: heartbreak without hatred — the tradition poisons even friendship.

chapters.title: Fourth Course: Honey
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Contestants are offered anything they want to walk away. Odile is promised her family's restored fortune; Xanthe, a full ride anywhere. Both refuse — Odile finally, fully, commits to Xanthe's side. Emotional beat: reconciliation through shared refusal.

chapters.title: The Undercroft
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Following the recipe box's hidden map, he finds the original audition chamber beneath the chapel: thirteen chairs, one empty since his grandmother fled. Here he learns the final course was meant to be given back — every winner returns their gained power to the town. Emotional beat: awe and clarity of purpose.

chapters.title: Fifth Course: Ash
chapters.summary: Headmaster Lark's POV. Lark, alarmed by Xanthe's discoveries, rewrites the fifth trial to eliminate him: contestants must burn one possession of another. Xanthe's grandmother's letters are seized. Watching them burn, Lark feels nothing — and notices he feels nothing. Emotional beat: the hollow center of power revealed.

chapters.title: Recitation
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Stripped of artifacts, Xanthe realizes memory lives in people, not paper. He recites his grandmother's stories to classmates across campus, rebuilding what was burned — and quietly recruiting the other fourteen contestants. Emotional beat: hope as collective act.

chapters.title: The Vote That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile calls a secret vote among contestants to restore the tradition's original rules. Lark's loyalists intimidate two voters; the motion fails by one. Odile is threatened with expulsion. Emotional beat: despair after near-victory.

chapters.title: Final Audition: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. At the final audition, Lark intends to crown himself steward-for-life using the rite's authority. Xanthe takes the empty thirteenth chair — claiming his grandmother's judgeship — and puts Lark's own conduct to the test the tradition demands. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into standing ground.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Judge
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Invoking the original final course — 'give it back' — Xanthe renounces his own winnings and calls on every heir in the room to do the same. One by one, contestants stand. Lark's authority dissolves not by force but by refusal. Emotional beat: triumphant surrender; power returned is power broken.

chapters.title: Aftertaste
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the aftermath, the town begins unscrambling its false history — painful, incomplete, real. Lark resigns rather than face the restored judges' council. Odile chooses to stay and help rebuild rather than flee to her family's money. Emotional beat: bruised, earned optimism.

chapters.title: Graduation
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Graduation day arrives and Xanthe stops counting days. He speaks briefly about inheritance — what we're given versus what we choose to carry. Milo apologizes; Xanthe doesn't absolve him so much as move forward beside him. Emotional beat: release.

chapters.title: The Seventeenth Yearbook
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, epilogue. A year later, Xanthe adds a new card to the recipe box — instructions for the next judge, honest ones — and leaves it where a frightened scholarship student will find it. The tradition continues, changed. Emotional beat: inheritance renewed; the story hands itself forward.
